note: The earliest surviving use of the word 'Trinity' (Greek trias) for the Godhead — c. AD 180, well before the creeds fixed the vocabulary. Key witness for the Trinity intro's 'before the creeds' point. Filed under Trinity (not deity) so it does not inflate the deity-of-Christ pre-Nicaea stat. text: In like manner also the three days which were before the luminaries, are types of the Trinity, of God, and His Word, and His wisdom.

author: Theophilus of Antioch
note: c. AD 180: Theophilus quotes John 1:1 by name ('one of whom, John, says'), an attribution of the Fourth Gospel's prologue to John before or alongside Irenaeus. Use ONLY for the attribution. The surrounding chapter carries Theophilus's pre-Nicene Logos vocabulary (the Word 'residing within the heart of God' and later 'uttered'), which compresses badly and can read as a temporal generation of the Son. Never quote that wider passage as our theology, and never present it as Nicene teaching. This note does NOT reach the live AI (api/ask.js sends only author/work/section/translation/text), so the truncation and the tags are the only runtime fence: never lengthen the excerpt, and never tag it trinity/deity/logos. The excerpt deliberately stops before John 1:1c; it is an attribution witness, not a witness to the verse's wording or to Christ's deity. Added 2026-11-15 from the Gathercole anonymity mine (backlog GATH-5); text copied from source_url. Verified verbatim vs source_url (apologia-citations, web, 2026-11-15).
text: And hence the holy writings teach us, and all the spirit-bearing [inspired] men, one of whom, John, says, In the beginning was the Word
